changed.title: Every permutation of w-bit states can be routed in four complete sweeps of a reversible shift register
changed.statement:
∀ d : ℕ,
  let w := d + 1
  let State := Fin w → Bool
  let Tail := Fin d → Bool
  ∀ perm : Equiv.Perm State,
    ∃ control : Fin (4 * w) → Tail → Bool,
      ∀ x : State, (List.finRange (4 * w)).foldl (fun (s : State) row =>
        let z : Tail := fun j => s j.succ
        Fin.snoc (α := fun _ : Fin w => Bool) z (xor (s 0) (control row z))) x = perm x
changed.unlocks: routes the prefix and suffix permutations needed for the physical-order lower bound on reversible counting
changed.context: Use L-lib-127 recursively to factor the reversal composed with the target into an ascending and a descending coordinate-switch sweep. Pad the second sweep by one identity layer. Run the ascending sweep in w physical shifts. Reverse the coordinates in two sweeps using the three XOR updates of a swap on each disjoint mirror pair. Run the descending switches in reversed coordinates in one forward sweep. Its physical output applies reversal to the chosen inner target, hence gives the requested permutation. The resource is reversible register rows.

changed.title: Eliminating free word coordinates in a parity coefficient of a local table count
changed.statement:
∀ (n r : Nat) (scope : Fin r → Finset (Fin n)),
  let Site := Fin n
  let Slot := Fin r × Finset Site
  let all := (Finset.univ : Finset Site)
  let slots := fun U : Finset Site => (Finset.univ : Finset Slot).filter
    (fun candidate => candidate.2 ⊆ scope candidate.1 ∩ U)
  let total := fun (U : Finset Site) (table : Finset Slot) =>
    (U.powerset.filter (fun x => ∀ i : Fin r, (i, x ∩ scope i) ∈ table)).card
  let coeff := fun (U : Finset Site) (M : Finset Slot) (g : Nat → Bool) =>
    ((M.powerset.filter (fun T => g (total U T))).card).testBit 0
  ∀ (U : Finset Site) (A : Finset Slot), A ⊆ slots U →
    let lift := (slots all).filter (fun s => (s.1, s.2 ∩ U) ∈ A)
    ∀ g : Nat → Bool, coeff all lift g =
      coeff U A (fun c => g (2^(n-U.card)*c))
changed.unlocks: reduces cyclic count coefficients to the coordinates meeting the missing entries
changed.context: Flip one site outside U in every word and its row patterns. The lift is invariant. The flip permutes its subtables without changing their counts, so paired subtables cancel mod two. Repeat on the fixed subtables for the other sites, since the flips commute. A surviving subtable contains whole fibers of the projection to U, hence comes from exactly one subtable of A. Each passing word on U then has exactly 2^(n-|U|) passing extensions.

changed.title: Weighted row sizes bound binary rank, with equality exactly for disjoint all-one diagonal blocks
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (w : Fin n → ℕ),
  (∀ i, G i i = true) → (∀ i, 0 < w i) →
  let M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod 2) :=
    fun a b => if G a b then 1 else 0
  let mass := fun (a : Fin n) => ∑ b : Fin n, if G a b then w b else 0
  let score : ℚ := ∑ i : Fin n, (w i : ℚ) / (mass i : ℚ)
  score ≤ (M.rank : ℚ) ∧
  (score = (M.rank : ℚ) ↔ ∀ i j, G i j = true → ∀ z, G i z = G j z)
changed.unlocks: bounds weighted reciprocal row masses by binary rank and characterizes every equality table
changed.context: Randomly order distinguishable tickets, w(i) per name, and order names by their initial ticket. Row i has pivot i with probability w(i)/mass(i). Rows whose initial one is their diagonal have distinct pivots. Equality forces their count to be rank in every order. Swapping the initial two names shows mutual adjacency. For adjacent i,j put any other z initial and swap i,j next: the count stays fixed only if z belongs to both rows or neither. Conversely each complete block contributes one pivot and one rank. Allow 2 to 4 hours.

changed.title: Successive constant output differences give exact fiber multiplicities on translation cosets of any binary vector map
changed.statement:
∀ (g t : ℕ),
  let F := ZMod 2
  let X := Fin g → F
  let Y := Fin t → F
  ∀ f : X → Y,
    let dirs := fun H : Submodule F Y =>
      {v : X | ∀ x : X, (f (x+v) - f x) - (f v - f 0) ∈ H}
    let grow := fun prior : Submodule F Y =>
      prior ⊔ Submodule.span F ((fun value : X => f value - f 0) '' dirs prior)
    let H := fun j : ℕ => (grow^[j]) (⊥ : Submodule F Y)
    H (t+1) = H t ∧
    ∀ (j : ℕ) (x : X) (y : Y),
      let num := Nat.card {v : X // v ∈ dirs (H j) ∧ f (x+v) = y}
      (y - f x ∈ H (j+1) → num * Nat.card ↥(H (j+1)) = Nat.card ↥(dirs (H j))) ∧
      (y - f x ∉ H (j+1) → num = 0)
changed.unlocks: Determines the exact multiplicity represented by each surviving quotient state when shifts of the output are exposed successively.
changed.context: The difference along a sum of two directions telescopes. Directions with constant difference modulo H therefore form a subspace and the induced shifts give a linear map into the output quotient. Its image is the enlarged H modulo H. Split each current input coset into previous input cosets. By induction each previous coset covers a full H-coset uniformly. The induced linear map sends equal numbers of these pieces to every new output residue. Multiply the two multiplicities. A strict output enlargement raises dimension, and equality is permanent.

changed.title: Exact adaptive parity query cost for recovering simultaneous products of binary affine forms with affine leaf outputs
changed.statement:
∀ (n t d : ℕ),
  let F := ZMod 2
  let V := Fin n → F
  let D := V →ₗ[F] F
  ∀ (a b c : Fin t → D) (u v e : Fin t → F),
    let target := fun (i : Fin t) (x : V) =>
      (a i x + u i) * (b i x + v i) + c i x + e i
    let run := fun (ask : Fin d → ℕ → D) (x : V) =>
      (List.finRange d).foldl (fun h j =>
        2 * h + (if ask j h x = 0 then 0 else 1)) (0 : ℕ)
    (∃ (ask : Fin d → ℕ → D) (readout : ℕ → Fin t → D)
        (bias : ℕ → Fin t → F),
      ∀ x i, target i x = readout (run ask x) i x + bias (run ask x) i) ↔
    (∃ pick : Fin t → D,
      (∀ i, pick i = a i ∨ pick i = b i ∨ pick i = a i + b i) ∧
      Module.finrank F (Submodule.span F (Set.range pick)) ≤ d)
changed.unlocks: determines the common parity-query depth needed to recover a family of binary quadratic products by affine outputs
changed.context: Follow the zero input. The whole common kernel of the questions on this path has the same transcript. If both factors restrict independently there, varying their two bits gives a nonzero mixed second difference, impossible for an affine leaf. Thus either factor or their sum vanishes on the kernel and lies in the span of the path questions. Conversely query a basis for the selected span. On each coset a factor is fixed or the factors differ by a constant. In each case the product reduces to an affine function.

changed.title: Local linear equations characterize all raw key shifts preserving any selected bits of both scheduled first-round words
changed.statement:
∀ (k : ℕ) [NeZero k],
  let I := ZMod k
  let B := ZMod 2
  let V := I → B
  let rot := fun (s : ℕ) (w : V) (i : I) => w (i-(s : I))
  let mix := fun (d : ℕ) (w : V) (i : I) => w (i-(d : I))+w i+w (i+(d : I))
  let out := fun (d u v : ℕ) (name c x : V) (j : I) =>
    let y := mix d (rot u x + name)
    y j + (1+y (j+1))*y (j+2) + rot v x j + c j
  let test := fun (d u v : ℕ) (z : V) (j : I) =>
    let a := mix d (rot u z)
    a j = rot v z j ∧ ((k = 1 ∨ k = 3) ∨ (a (j+1) = 0 ∧ a (j+2) = 0))
  ∀ (row col cr cc z : V) (S T : Finset I),
    (∀ x : V,
      (∀ j ∈ S, out 1 1 0 row cr (x+z) j = out 1 1 0 row cr x j) ∧
      (∀ i ∈ T, out 2 3 4 col cc (x+z) i = out 2 3 4 col cc x i)) ↔
    (∀ j ∈ S, test 1 1 0 z j) ∧ (∀ i ∈ T, test 2 3 4 z i)
changed.unlocks: Computes the exact period space of arbitrary requested first-round bits directly from the two tap stencils. It gives the raw key parity lower bound for overlapping windows.
changed.context: Write a for the mixed shift and y for the mixed word. The change at j has variable part a(j+2)y(j+1)+a(j+1)y(j+2). Each mixed coordinate is a nonzero form on the key. Adjacent forms are distinct unless all translates of the tap mask agree. At widths above three a nonzero mask of at most three sites cannot be constant. At width two the mix is the identity. Hence both coefficients must vanish, leaving a(j) equal to the reinjected shift. At widths one and three y is constant across sites, so the nonlinear product vanishes identically. Intersect the requested tests.

Hence both coefficients must vanish, leaving a(j) equal to the reinjected shift. At widths one and three y is constant across sites, so the nonlinear product vanishes identically. Intersect the requested tests.

changed.title: The optimal worst-case success and largest seed weight for randomized fan-in-two inner-product predictors
changed.statement:
let nonlinear := fun (g : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate) =>
  (g.inputs.length == 2) &&
  xor (xor (g.op.eval [false,false]) (g.op.eval [false,true]))
      (xor (g.op.eval [true,false]) (g.op.eval [true,true]))
∀ s t : ℕ, t ≤ s →
  let N := 2^(2*s)
  let h : ℕ := 2^(s-t)
  let valid := fun (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
    (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.inputs.length ≤ 2) ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (N+N) C ∧ C.gates.countP nonlinear ≤ t
  let value := fun (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (x y : Fin N) =>
    C.eval (PEqualNP.Represents.oneEach x y)
  let target := fun (i j : Fin N) =>
    ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin (2*s))).filter (fun b =>
      i.val.testBit b.val && j.val.testBit b.val)).card % 2 == 1
  (∀ (l : ℕ) (Cs : Fin l → PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (p : Fin l → ℚ),
    (∀ i, valid (Cs i)) → (∀ i, 0 ≤ p i) → (∑ i, p i) = 1 →
    let success := fun (x y : Fin N) =>
      ∑ i : Fin l, if value (Cs i) x y = target x y then p i else 0
    (∃ x y, 2*(h : ℚ)*success x y ≤ (h : ℚ)+1) ∧
    ((∀ x y, (h : ℚ)+1 ≤ 2*(h : ℚ)*success x y) →
      ∀ i, (h : ℚ)^2 * p i ≤ 1)) ∧
  ∃ Cs : Fin (h^2) → PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, (∀ z, valid (Cs z)) ∧
    ∀ x y, 2*h*((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin (h^2))).filter
      (fun z => value (Cs z) x y = target x y)).card = (h+1)*h^2
changed.unlocks: prices the minimum support of a finite lottery attaining optimal prediction probability on each inner-product input
changed.context: Use affine port labels to bound the sign matrix rank by m. Project H onto the range of each prediction. Cauchy-Schwarz bounds correlation and saturation gives K_i=h P_i H. Pointwise equality yields a tight weighted sum of projections. Apply the projection weight bound to get mass at most one over h squared on each positive atom. Pair dot coordinates with one product per pair, then translate the residual columns uniformly and add the local row correction. This attains the stated bias on every cell. Allow 3 to 5 hours.

changed.title: The Boolean degree of each second-channel image bounds the number of common words per third-channel tag
changed.statement:
∀ (k r c : ℕ),
  let F := ZMod 2
  let X := Fin k → F
  let Z := Fin r → F
  let W := X × Z
  ∀ (send : W → X) (tag : W → Fin c → Bool),
    (∀ a b t : W, a.1 = b.1 → send b = send t → tag t = tag a → a = b ∧ b = t) →
    let volume := fun d : ℕ => ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (min k d + 1), k.choose j
    (∀ d : ℕ,
      (∀ u : X, ∃ coeff : Finset (Fin k) → F, ∀ y : X,
        (∑ S ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun S : Finset (Fin k) => S.card ≤ d),
          coeff S * ∏ j ∈ S, y j) =
        (if y ∈ Finset.univ.image (fun z : Z => send (u,z)) then (1 : F) else 0)) →
      (∀ h : Fin c → Bool, (Finset.univ.filter (fun w : W => tag w = h)).card ≤ volume d) ∧
      2^(k+r) ≤ 2^c * volume d) ∧
    ((∀ u : X, ∃ (A : Z →ₗ[F] X) (v : X), ∀ z : Z, send (u,z) = A z + v) →
      r ≤ k ∧ 2^(k+r) ≤ 2^c * volume (k-r))
changed.unlocks: bounds the number of words per tag before optimizing the conditional affine witness
changed.context: Fix a third tag. Two distinct words with this tag cannot share a short endpoint or have a cross pair in the image, since that pair supplies a middle word. The row-image indicators, evaluated at the selected second strings, give an identity matrix. Degree-d indicators lie in the span of the square-free monomials of size at most d, bounding each tag class by that dimension. Sum over tags. Affine suffix maps are injective in each row. Their images have codimension k-r and membership is a product of k-r affine tests.

changed.title: An erroneous pooled decoder on uniform copies restricts to half the base types with a quadratic saving in errors
changed.statement:
∀ (n b q : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n), 0 < b →
  ∀ (rowCap colCap : Fin q → ℕ),
  let fits := fun (s : ℕ) (G : Fin s → Fin s → Bool) (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin s)) (E : ℕ) =>
    ∃ (rf cf : Fin s → Bool) (R C : Fin q → Finset (Fin s))
      (out : Finset (Fin s) → (Fin q → Bool) → Bool),
      (∀ t, (R t).card ≤ rowCap t ∧ (C t).card ≤ colCap t) ∧
      ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin s × Fin s)).filter (fun z =>
        out {z.1,z.2} (fun t => decide (z.1 ∈ R t ∨ π z.2 ∈ C t)) ≠
          Bool.xor (G z.1 (π z.2)) (Bool.xor (rf z.1) (cf (π z.2))))).card ≤ E
  let typ := fun label : Fin (n*b) => (⟨label.val % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩ : Fin n)
  let h := (n+1)/2
  ∀ (G : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin (n*b))) (E : ℕ),
    fits (n*b) (fun x y => G (typ x) (typ y)) π E →
    ∃ row col : Fin h ↪ Fin n,
      fits h (fun x y => G (row x) (col y)) (Equiv.refl _) (4*E/b^2)
changed.unlocks: A lower bound on every half-sized matched subtable now transfers to all copy counts with a constant error-density loss.
changed.context: Sample one physical matched name uniformly and independently at each row type. In any column type the hit probabilities from the rows sum to one, so its miss probability is at most exp(-1)<3/8. The expected distinct column count exceeds 5n/8. With probability at least 1/4 it reaches ceil(n/2). Retain one representative per chosen type. Restrict pins and flips and correct singleton diagonals. An erroneous off-diagonal cell is retained with probability at most 1/b² before conditioning. Average on the good event.

changed.title: A logarithmic binary rank forces crossed parity errors on every matching covering half the types
changed.statement:
∀ coreBits : ℕ, 16 ≤ coreBits →
  let n := 2^coreBits
  let h := n/2
  let F := ZMod 2
  let W := Fin (32*coreBits) → F
  ∃ u v : Fin n → W,
    ∀ (row col : Fin h ↪ Fin n) (q : ℕ), 256*coreBits*3^q ≤ n →
    ∀ (color : Fin h → Fin (3^q)) (sign : Fin h → F),
      let dot := fun (x y : W) => ∑ j : Fin (32*coreBits), x j * y j
      let bad := ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin h × Fin h)).filter (fun z =>
        z.1 < z.2 ∧ color z.1 = color z.2 ∧
          dot (u (row z.1)) (v (col z.2)) + dot (u (row z.2)) (v (col z.1)) ≠
            sign z.1 + sign z.2)).card
      h^2 < 4096*3^q*bad
changed.unlocks: The bound applies after keeping arbitrary halves of the two banks, which makes error density survive replication at an absolute constant.
changed.context: Use columns with 8a independent vectors in each 32a-set. Fix both injections, colors and signs. In classes of size at least h/(4C), sample 32a testers, C=3^q. At least h/2 other rows give M≥4ah independent fair tests after conditioning. A low-loss book gives sampled loss ≤ah/8 with chance at least half. Weight the binomial sum at 1/16; (17/16)^8<2 gives a tail ≤2^(-3ah). There are at most n^(2h) C^h 2^h configurations per q, with C≤n/4. The union over at most a+1 budgets has probability below one.

At least h/2 other rows give M≥4ah independent fair tests after conditioning. A low-loss book gives sampled loss ≤ah/8 with chance at least half. Weight the binomial sum at 1/16; (17/16)^8<2 gives a tail ≤2^(-3ah). There are at most n^(2h) C^h 2^h configurations per q, with C≤n/4. The union over at most a+1 budgets has probability below one.

changed.title: One pair of small feature tables forces an inverse-exponential pooled error fraction at every larger address width
changed.statement:
∀ coreBits : ℕ, 16 ≤ coreBits →
  let m := 2^coreBits
  let F := ZMod 2
  let W := Fin (32*coreBits) → F
  ∃ u v : Fin m → W, ∀ k : ℕ, coreBits ≤ k →
    let N := 2^k
    let I := Fin N
    let typ := fun label : I => Fin.ofNat m label.val
    let G := fun x y : I => decide ((∑ j : Fin (32*coreBits), u (typ x) j * v (typ y) j) = 1)
    PEqualNP.Represents.HasLitSize (k+k) (PEqualNP.Represents.adjFun (k := k) (l := k) G)
      (1024*m) ∧
    ∀ q : ℕ, 256*coreBits*3^q ≤ m →
      ∀ (π : Equiv.Perm I) (rf cf : I → Bool) (R C : Fin q → Finset I)
        (out : Finset I → (Fin q → Bool) → Bool),
      let E := ((Finset.univ : Finset (I × I)).filter (fun z =>
        out {z.1,z.2} (fun t => decide (z.1 ∈ R t ∨ π z.2 ∈ C t)) ≠
          Bool.xor (G z.1 (π z.2)) (Bool.xor (rf z.1) (cf (π z.2))))).card
      N^2 < 65536*3^q*E
changed.unlocks: Provides a linear binary-address circuit family with an inverse-3^q lower bound on the error fraction at every larger address width.
changed.context: Fix factors hard on every matching of half the m types. Low address bits give b=2^(k-a) copies of each type. Restrict any E-error decoder to m/2 paired types with at most 4E/b² errors. Normalize each pool to a ternary digit and combine the switches on each label. Each equal-word parity conflict forces one error. Substitute the half-matching lower bound and N=bm. The shared lookup on 32a features costs at most 776m+256a+4≤1024m on any larger width.

Restrict any E-error decoder to m/2 paired types with at most 4E/b² errors. Normalize each pool to a ternary digit and combine the switches on each label. Each equal-word parity conflict forces one error. Substitute the half-matching lower bound and N=bm. The shared lookup on 32a features costs at most 776m+256a+4≤1024m on any larger width.
